script.base: Buffalo should lead at home as a 7.5-point favorite (implied totals BUF 28.5 / NE 21.0) in a 49.5 game, but New England's run defense (3.52 YPC, only 8 runs of 10+ in 4 games) should stop James Cook from turning that lead into a 112-yard night. The path to 28.5 is Josh Allen throwing: Dalton Kincaid is the target leader (14 targets, 131 yards, 107 air yards in weeks 2-4) into a pass defense allowing 8.67 YPA in the middle and 16 passes of 20+. New England, as a 7.5-point dog, throws more; Maye has been better vs the blitz (0.36 EPA/db) than clean (0.25), and Buffalo has allowed only 5 passes of 20+.
script.flip1: New England hangs around or leads behind Maye's legs (17 carries, 90 yards in weeks 2-4) and the Stevenson/Henderson committee. Buffalo cannot clock-kill, Cook's late carries stall, and Allen's pass volume rises further. Cook under and Kincaid over both still live, but a track meet raises the chance Cook rips the explosive that busts 112.5.
script.flip2: Buffalo jumps ahead by 14+ early and the run actually works. Cook's carries climb into the mid-20s and can clear 112.5 even at modest YPC, while Kincaid gets scripted out after halftime. Garbage time would then be New England throwing (Henry/Diggs), not Buffalo skill players.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Cook under lost because he is not an average runner into an average 3.52: the 132, 108 and 117 already happened, Williams and Tavai sat, and 22 carries at 5.2 YPC walked through 112.5 in a clock-killing home win. We had no opponent splits to prove the run-defense number would travel. Kincaid over lost because the middle targets went to Shakir (L3 games 12, 45, 69) and Coleman, Knox vultured the red zone, and Buffalo still ran enough that Allen did not need 14 targets to his tight end. The 28- and 37-yard games are half the card, 42.5 is just the median, and we never saw a price. That counter is strong enough to keep Kincaid a lean, not a strong leg. It is not stronger than Cook's structural math, which still needs both a full load and near-5.8 YPC unless inactives confirm the front is short.
